pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Black Sigatoka is caused by the plant-pathogenic fungus Mycosphaerella fijiensis

type_of_disease.quote: Two fungal pathogens cause similar but slightly different Sigatoka diseases. Black Sigatoka or black leaf streak (BLS) is the most important fungal disease of banana

affected_parts.quote: This infection will form lesions on the undersurface of the leaf. Although both Black and Yellow Sigatoka form leaf streaks

summary.value: Black streaks and spots on leaves that cause reduced photosynthesis and defoliation, severely reducing banana bunch yield and fruit quality.
summary.quote: through reduced photosynthesis and defoliation can severely reduce banana bunch yield and fruit quality. BLS's early streaks and spots streaks are black

diagnostic_features.value: Black streaks and spots that lack the distinct yellow halo characteristic of Yellow Sigatoka.
diagnostic_features.quote: BLS's early streaks and spots streaks are black and lack the distinct yellow halo that is present in young streaks of yellow Sigatoka

look_alikes.quote: Although both Black and Yellow Sigatoka form leaf streaks, BLS's early streaks and spots streaks are black and lack the distinct yellow halo that is present in young streaks of yellow Sigatoka

affected_parts.quote: affects even the immature fruits... The upper portion of the peduncle is exposed... spreads to fingers... Dry rot also occurs in the pulp

summary.value: The infection causes blackening of fruit skin with shrinkage and folding of tissues, which become corrugated and covered with powdery grey conidia resembling ash. Dry rot develops in the pulp, making affected tissues dry and fibrous.
summary.quote: The infection, which occurs in perianth, spreads to fingers causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of the tissues. The affected tissues are corrugated and covered with conidiophores and powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end. Dry rot also occurs in the pulp and the affected tissues become dry and fibrous.

diagnostic_features.value: Corrugated tissues covered with powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end
diagnostic_features.quote: The affected tissues are corrugated and covered with conidiophores and powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Two Neocordana species are responsible for Cordana leaf spot symptoms: Neocordana musae, formerly Cordana musea and originally described as Scoletrichum musae; and Neocordana johnstonii, formerly Cordana johnstonii

type_of_disease.quote: It is caused by two Neocordana fungi

affected_parts.quote: The most characteristic symptoms of the disease are on the leaf.

summary.value: Large, pale brown, oval to fusiform necrotic lesions with pale grey concentric ring patterns and dark brown borders surrounded by bright yellow halos. Lesions coalesce into large necrotic patches, and leaves ultimately turn brown and dry out.
summary.quote: They are large, pale brown, oval to fusiform necrotic lesions with pale grey concentric ring patterns, with a dark brown border surrounded by a bright yellow halo separating the lesion from the healthy leaf tissue. Often, lesions coalesce into large necrotic patches. The leaves ultimately turn brown and dry out.

diagnostic_features.value: Pale grey concentric ring patterns with dark brown border surrounded by bright yellow halo. Spots caused by N. musae are larger and oval to elliptical, while N. johnstonii spots are smaller and become more fusiform with age. Spores produced in large quantities on the underside of leaves, appearing as greyish-brown and hairy.
diagnostic_features.quote: with pale grey concentric ring patterns, with a dark brown border surrounded by a bright yellow halo separating the lesion from the healthy leaf tissue. The leaf spots caused by N. musae are larger and oval to elliptical in shape, while those caused by N. johnstonii are generally smaller and become more fusiform with age.

conflicts.alternative_value: Cordana musae (Neocordana musae) and Cordana johnstonii (Neocordana johnstonii)
conflicts.note: Bayer lists the older Cordana names as primary with Neocordana in parentheses; Promusa uses Neocordana as the current accepted names, consistent with modern taxonomy.
